title: Integrate overload protection with cost-efficient batching tier (backpressure thresholds + load-shed reason codes)
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Title: Integrate overload protection with cost-efficient batching tier (backpressure thresholds + load-shed reason codes)

Context
Cost-efficient tier intentionally increases batching aggressiveness (larger max_batch, longer queue delay) to improve $/token. During internal dogfooding and early beta ramps we observed that under bursty concurrency, the same aggressiveness can push the system into a “latency spiral” (queue delay grows, timeouts increase, retries amplify load) unless overload protection thresholds are tier-aware and we emit actionable reason codes. This PR wires tier selection into the existing overload protection module and adds explicit load-shed reason codes + metrics hooks so SRE dashboards can distinguish “expected shedding” vs regressions.

What’s in this PR
- Tier-aware overload thresholds
  - When batching_tier == cost_efficient, apply more conservative backpressure earlier (lower admission watermark, stricter queue-delay caps) to avoid tail-latency blowups.
  - When batching_tier == fast, preserve existing behavior (minimal queueing) and avoid false positives for streaming routes.
  - Standard tier remains the current baseline.
- Load-shed reason codes (request-facing + metrics)
  - Introduces a stable set of shed reasons with consistent naming across gateway/runtime:
    - queue_delay_budget_exceeded
    - gpu_kv_cache_pressure
    - inflight_requests_cap
    - prefill_backlog
    - decode_backlog
    - scheduler_deadline_miss
  - Adds response header for internal debugging and Console integration:
    - x-redwood-load-shed-reason: <reason>
  - Tracing span attribute:
    - redwood.overload.shed_reason
- Metrics / dashboard hooks
  - Counter: redwood_overload_shed_total{tier,route,model,reason}
  - Gauge: redwood_overload_backpressure_active{tier,route,model}
  - Histogram: redwood_overload_admission_queue_delay_ms{tier,route,model}
  - These align with the tiered batching dashboard spec; the intent is that SRE can alert on rate-of-shed and reason mix shifts rather than raw 5xx alone.
- Policy/guardrail integration
  - Adds tier to overload protection context so that guardrail rules can branch on tier without re-deriving it.
  - Ensures explicit batching overrides do not bypass overload protection; overload protection acts on effective scheduler state, not config intent.

Behavioral changes
- In cost-efficient tier, when queue delay exceeds the tier-specific budget for the route, we begin load shedding sooner rather than letting latency drift into timeouts.
- For streaming routes, we bias toward inflight caps and decode backlog detection rather than queue delay alone (prevents over-shedding while token cadence is healthy).

Defaults / thresholds (initial)
- cost_efficient:
  - admission_watermark: 0.80 (was 0.90)
  - queue_delay_budget_ms: 200 (chat), 300 (completions), 100 (embeddings)
  - kv_cache_pressure_shed_at: 0.88 (was 0.92)
- standard: unchanged
- fast:
  - queue_delay_budget_ms remains low; shedding primarily via inflight cap and deadline misses

Notes:
- These are intentionally conservative. The goal is to reduce timeouts during bursts by shedding earlier with clear reason codes; tuning will happen post-beta with benchmarks + canary data.

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - Tier-specific threshold selection and precedence
  - Reason code mapping stability and serialization to header/span
- Integration tests:
  - Synthetic overload scenarios validate shed behavior does not regress fast tier streaming cadence
  - Cost-efficient tier under burst: shed_total increases while timeout rate decreases
- Manual:
  - Verified dashboards ingestion in staging (metrics labels present: tier,reason)

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: runtime.overload.tier_aware_thresholds (default off).
- Enable in staging for 48h; verify reason mix and no increase in overall 5xx.
- Canary production: 5% of traffic for cost-efficient tier only in us-east for two launch models.
- Abort signals:
  - p95 latency up > 10% for fast/standard
  - timeout_rate up > 0.2% absolute
  - shed_total spike without corresponding reduction in timeouts (indicates misconfigured thresholds)

Changed areas (high level)
- runtime/overload/
  - add TieredThresholds and policy context plumbed from effective config
- runtime/scheduler/
  - exposes scheduler backlog signals required for decode_backlog/prefill_backlog reasons
- api-gateway/
  - forwards x-redwood-load-shed-reason on 429/503 from runtime
- observability/
  - metric definitions and labels

Illustrative snippet (reason code)
- Before: shed_reason = "overloaded"
- After: shed_reason = "queue_delay_budget_exceeded" | "gpu_kv_cache_pressure" | ...

Related
- Linear: ENG-18424 (overload protection alignment), ENG-18422 (queue delay & batch formation metrics)
- Reference: Support escalation SUP-18492 (timeouts when trying cost-efficient tier; this PR is part of the fix by preventing timeout spirals)

Checklist
- [x] Added tests for tier mapping and reason codes
- [x] Added metrics with tier + reason labels
- [x] Updated internal runbook notes in code comments (SRE will link in dashboards spec)
- [x] No API breaking changes (header is additive)

Commits
1) runtime/overload: introduce tier-aware thresholds and reason enum
2) runtime/scheduler: export backlog signals and wire to overload module
3) gateway: propagate shed reason header for 429/503
4) observability: add metrics + label set, update exporters
5) tests: unit + integration coverage, add golden tests for reason strings

Review conversation (highlights)
- Sofia Ivanova: “Can we avoid queue_delay as the primary signal for streaming? It’s too noisy when clients disconnect/reconnect.”
  - Jordan Lee: Switched streaming routes to prefer decode_backlog and inflight caps; queue delay budget still enforced but de-prioritized. Added integration test that asserts no increased shed rate during healthy cadence.
- Rafael Mendes: “Reason code strings need to be stable for alerting; please add a golden test and doc comment that they’re part of the contract.”
  - Jordan Lee: Added golden test for all reason enum values and a contract comment + linter check that forbids renames without updating the golden file.
- Allison Grant: “Metrics need tier and reason labels; also please add a separate gauge for backpressure active.”
  - Jordan Lee: Added redwood_overload_backpressure_active and updated counter label set.
- Nadia Rahman: “We should be careful that earlier shedding doesn’t increase retries and overall cost; do we have visibility?”
  - Jordan Lee: Added shed reason header to make client-side retry debugging easier; also added a note for Optimize/Console to surface shed reasons so customers can adjust client retry behavior.

CI
- Initial run: perf-smoke failed (flake in scheduler backlog test)
- Rerun: pass
- Final checks: buildkite/runtime-tests ✅, buildkite/gateway-tests ✅, lint ✅, perf-smoke ✅

Merge
Squash merged to main. Follow-up items: tune thresholds per model family/GPU SKU and wire dashboard panels to new reason breakdown (tracked in ENG-18427).
release_notes:
- Runtime: tier-aware overload protection thresholds for cost-efficient batching tier (flagged)
- Observability: overload shedding metrics now include tier and shed reason labels; adds x-redwood-load-shed-reason header for debugging
